FR-D1: partly built: the builder-to-gate hand-off in kernel/dispatch.py is pinned to revisions (each round's patch is a commit recorded as cell_ran with its head, the gate's objections are recorded against that head, and the next envelope names the contract and base revisions and carries them); open questions and decisions live in the canon, signals in the factory's signals.json, lessons in each project's lessons.json, verifier findings in the gate's native values. not built: one typed workspace that every hand-off between cells passes through. The hand-off itself is passed in memory and only recorded as a side effect, the artifacts are scattered over unrelated stores with no common type or revision pin, nothing supersedes or links an artifact to another, and there is no finding, failure record or seam contract artifact type. It would take a workspace store (artifact type, revision, supersedes, links) that cells read their inputs from and write their outputs to, with the envelope built from it.
FR-D2: partly built: every repair round (head, verdict, objections) is appended to the project's hash-chained ledger, each envelope carries only the previous round's objections, a retried task starts with none, and a person's workspace reads earlier rounds by reference through the MCP ledger resource. not built: a ledger of paths tried as such, recording the approaches and dead ends of scouts and builders across tasks and lanes; a builder cell has no way to consult earlier paths by reference (its lane has no MCP server and the envelope names no ledger entries), and the escalation card keeps only the last round's objections.
FR-D3: not built: there is no typed workspace to bypass, so no edge between cells is modelled, detected or shown, and nothing in the kernel, cockpit or MCP server raises an invariant breach. Lanes prevent some edges (one holder per lane; checkout removes untracked files) but keep .gnomon-sessions/ and .gnomon-audit/ from earlier cells in the same lane unchecked. It would take recording each cell's inputs and outputs as workspace artifacts, comparing them with the workspace's edges after each run, and opening an invariant-breach card and cockpit alert on any mismatch.
